technical_and_design_decisions: Implement the GemFire messaging integration as a Spring Cloud Stream binder using GemFire regions and eventing mechanisms, with configurable region names, serialization, consumer groups, and producer/consumer properties.
Use existing Spring Cloud Data Flow SPI extension points for GemFire-backed stream storage and module registration rather than introducing a parallel orchestration model.
Represent stream definitions and deployment metadata in GemFire regions, with explicit handling for consistency, serialization, versioning, and concurrent updates.
Implement the module registry as a GemFire-backed registry that stores module metadata and artifact coordinates and exposes the interfaces expected by Spring Cloud Data Flow.
Implement taps as additional consumers or derived GemFire subscriptions so that tap processing does not alter or interrupt the primary pipeline.
Expose tap creation and management through the Data Flow DSL and shell while preserving compatibility with existing stream and task commands.
Use Java 17 and the Spring Framework/Spring Cloud APIs supported by the target project version.
Provide automated unit tests, contract tests, and integration tests against a locally provisioned GemFire-compatible test environment.
Document deployment manifests, partition-related configuration, directly bound modules, and tap usage with runnable examples.
assumptions: The increment is implemented in an existing Spring Cloud Stream/Data Flow codebase with established build conventions, extension points, and test infrastructure.
GemFire client libraries, connection configuration, authentication mechanisms, and a testable GemFire or Apache Geode-compatible environment are available or can be provisioned locally.
The specification does not require changes to GemFire itself, the Spring Framework core, or unrelated Data Flow components.
The GemFire SPI, stream repository, and module registry can be implemented using existing Spring Cloud Data Flow interfaces; any required interface additions are limited and backward compatible.
The incomplete wording of U5 is interpreted as requiring documentation for deployment manifests, partition configuration, and deployment of streams involving partitioned GemFire resources.
Direct binding documentation is an example-focused documentation change and does not require a new direct-binding runtime feature beyond existing launcher behavior.
Tap support requires both backend/runtime support and Data Flow DSL/Shell commands or syntax, but does not include a new graphical user interface.
Security, multi-region disaster recovery, cross-data-center replication, performance certification, and production operations runbooks are outside the increment.
Effort includes implementation, code review preparation, automated testing, documentation, and developer-level defect correction, but excludes elapsed waiting time and work by other teams.

activities.activity_description: Inspect the existing Spring Cloud Stream and Spring Cloud Data Flow modules, identify applicable extension points, trace relevant APIs, clarify the incomplete documentation requirement, and produce an implementation checklist for U1-U8.

Design GemFire region usage, message serialization, event delivery, consumer groups, partitioning, persistence, registry and repository data models, tap isolation, configuration properties, compatibility behavior, and error handling.

activities.activity_name: GemFire Spring Cloud Stream message-channel binder
activities.activity_description: Implement producer and consumer endpoints, GemFire connection and region configuration, message conversion, headers, consumer groups, partition-aware routing, lifecycle management, error handling, and binder configuration metadata.

Implement the GemFire-specific SPI adapters required by Spring Cloud Data Flow, including service configuration, connection management, health behavior, and integration with the Data Flow orchestration lifecycle.

Implement persistence and retrieval of stream definitions and related metadata in GemFire, including serialization, identifiers, update/delete behavior, concurrency handling, and repository integration tests.
Implement module registration, lookup, metadata persistence, version handling, removal, and compatibility with Data Flow module discovery and deployment operations.

Implement creation and management of taps on primary pipelines, additional GemFire subscriptions or derived channels, tap lifecycle behavior, naming and cleanup rules, and safeguards ensuring the original stream is not impacted.

activities.activity_name: Data Flow DSL and Shell tap support
activities.activity_description: Add tap syntax, command parsing, validation, command execution, status/listing behavior, help text, error reporting, and compatibility tests for DSL and Shell workflows.
Document deployment manifests, GemFire connection and region configuration, partition-related settings, stream deployment examples, constraints, and troubleshooting guidance.
Document directly bound modules, launcher usage, command-line arguments, aggregate deployment, binding configuration, and the supplied filter pipeline example.

Add unit, integration, contract, persistence, partitioning, serialization, lifecycle, tap isolation, DSL, Shell, and failure-path tests; provision and execute tests against a GemFire-compatible environment.

activities.activity_name: Build, packaging, configuration metadata, and compatibility updates
activities.activity_description: Update Maven modules, dependency management, auto-configuration, configuration metadata, test profiles, release packaging, and CI setup required to build and exercise the increment.

activities.activity_name: Code review preparation, defect correction, and final integration
activities.activity_description: Perform self-review, resolve integration defects, improve diagnostics and documentation, run the complete verification suite, and prepare the final increment for merge and release.
